feedback: Written before this candidate races. Race 8 (entityR2B, 742.12) is the best result: body_length 0.12 m gave oval 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.221, s-bend 20/20, and slalom 2/20 finishes with line loss down from 1.2 to 1.0. That supports yaw inertia as part of the slalom limit, though not as the whole cause. Race 3 (235.88) and race 6 (389.47) already ruled out reach and density, so the yaw-response test is well-motivated. The wheel_track 0.10 change is a sound single-variable step. The Integrator has rescaled kp to 2.7 and kd to 0.5, so this is a fair test of yaw authority. The candidate's outcome is not known yet. Once race 9 reports: if slalom line loss falls below 1, keep wheel_track 0.10 and tune base_speed. If slalom line loss is unchanged or worse, yaw authority is not the limit, and the next step is controller response, not more geometry. Note that max_error on slalom was 0.0594 in race 8, close to the 0.06 limit, so small drift changes can flip finishes.
requested_changes: Keep the race 8 platform (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.06, body_length 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg) and change only wheel_track to 0.10 m, with the Integrator's kp 2.7 and kd 0.5 rescale, so the result can be read against race 8.
If slalom line loss stays at 1 or more after this race, hold the geometry and let the Integrator adjust kd and base_speed. Do not add further geometry in the same step.

Exploration only, if the slalom result is clear and it still does not finish: test mass at the low end (0.6 kg), since lower mass also cuts yaw inertia and adds traction-limited turning. This needs its own race and should not be combined with the wheel_track change.
